blind_target.title: Brain aging in major depressive disorder: results from the ENIGMA major depressive disorder working group.
blind_target.outcome_quote: This replication study using data from 13 cohorts around the world confirmed our previous findings that persons with major depressive disorder show advanced brain aging compared to controls by approximately +1 year.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Overall conclusion explicitly confirms the original brain-age gap using new independent cohorts. Cohort heterogeneity does not override that verdict.

luna_triage.reason: The empirical retest of Han et al. (2021a) is explicit and concerns the same brain-age gap described in supplied row 799. However, row 799 is a 2018 conference abstract with a different title and DOI, and the supplied materials do not establish that it is the same original work/report as the 2021a article. Need bibliographic/report-equivalence evidence before treating it as represented or an omission.
luna_triage.omission_quote: Importantly, we aim to contribute to the growing area of brain age research by attempting to replicate the magnitude of the brain age gap difference previously reported by the ENIGMA-MDD consortium between persons with depression (N = 766) and controls (N = 751) using this method.
luna_triage.identity_quote: Our previous ENIGMA MDD consortium study, the largest study of brain age in depression to date (N = 2126 controls and N = 2675 patients), showed a +1.08 year higher brain-PAD in depression

quality_gate: Luna is triage only. Independently establish actual empirical retesting and absence under ALL shipped identities/alternate reports. Read prior objections. No paper outcome is being requested.
